sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 Oct 2025): a leaked omnibus draft (the '11th Judicial Package') would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise LGBT conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' (up to 3 years), criminalise same-sex ceremonies (up to 4 years), raise the age for gender-affirming healthcare to 25 with mandatory infertility and multiple-evaluation conditions, and punish providers with fines and up to 7 years' imprisonment; 15 LGBT groups and the national medical association object.

Kaos GL (24 Feb 2026) on its LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, 'The Year of the Family: A Major Siege': in 2025 hostility became explicit state policy (presidency-centred; a family ministry as implementing body; religious-authority and broadcasting-regulator restrictions; one LGBTI+ organisation closed); 6 right-to-life violations documented (3 recorded as hate-motivated, trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 the previous year), 313 liberty violations (~2.5x the previous year); official hate-crime statistics are not kept.

records.name: Karaman
records.current_summary: Conservative interior province province. No province-specific trans-related findings in this research pass; the national framework and its 2025-26 escalation apply here unchanged. The region's own sources are national-level: a leaked draft omnibus reform package (11th Judicial Package, October 2025) would create new anti-LGBT articles — criminalising conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality", restricting gender-affirming healthcare with a minimum age of 25, and enabling charges against trans people and their providers; the state's "Year of the Family" institutional programme and blanket bans on LGBTI public events are national practice, not provincial choices. Per the country research dossier, the absence of a documented provincial ban here is not evidence of tolerance — the national blanket-ban practice applies across the country.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 October 2025): a leaked draft omnibus reform package — the 11th Judicial Package — would amend the penal and civil codes with new anti-LGBT articles: criminalising behaviour "contrary to biological sex and general morality" including its so-called "promotion", raising the minimum age for gender-affirming healthcare to 25 with onerous eligibility conditions, and enabling criminal charges against trans people and the medical professionals who treat them. HRW called for immediate withdrawal of the package.

Kaos GL Association's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 (published February 2026; monitoring since 2007), titled "The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People": in 2025 anti-LGBTI policies became institutionalised — instructions to public institutions under the "Year of the Family" banner plus religious and administrative rhetoric from senior officials created a climate that encouraged human-rights violations. National monitoring based on media-documented violations and civil-society applications.

records.name: Kilis
records.current_summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): border; conservative. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 October 2025): a leaked draft omnibus reform (the '11th Judicial Package') would amend the penal code so that acting 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' — or its promotion — carries up to three years in prison (an amendment to article 225 on 'indecent acts'), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under onerous eligibility rules, and allow criminal charges against trans people and the professionals who treat them; justified as protecting 'the family' and 'public morals'. HRW called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks of the decade and urged withdrawal.

Kaos GL (24 February 2026): presentation of its 'LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025', titled 'The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People'. Findings: anti-LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — targeting of LGBTI+ people as 'deviant' or 'a threat' by the president and senior officials raised officials' motivation and third-party impunity; the new Family Ministry became the implementing ministry; one LGBTI+ rights organisation was closed; platforms and broadcasters were penalised or withdrew; artistic events were cancelled. The report documents six violations of the right to life (three hate-motivated killings; trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 the previous year, largely during assemblies) and 313 liberty violations in 2025 (about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions). No official hate-crime statistics exist; cases rely on media.
